title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government is responding to the Committee’s 2020 report on AI and Public Standards, aiming to strengthen accountability, transparency, and safety in AI systems. It outlines measures such as new regulations, oversight mechanisms, and public engagement initiatives to ensure AI technologies meet societal expectations and protect citizens.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has set out its plan to regulate how artificial intelligence can be used in the qualifications sector, ensuring that any AI tools support fair and reliable assessment. The policy was issued at the request of the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright laws affect the development of AI, looking at how copyrighted works are used to train and improve AI systems. It evaluates the legal and ethical implications of this practice, offering guidance for creators, developers, and policymakers.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining its plans to strengthen regulation, boost innovation, and invest in skills and research to keep the country competitive. It emphasises a balanced approach that protects public safety, promotes ethical use of AI, and supports businesses in adopting responsible AI technologies.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the terms of reference for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes FAQs that clarify the committee’s purpose, scope, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into AI governance. The document likely outlines CSPL’s views on how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence will shape the rules that govern medical products, aiming to ensure safety and effectiveness while keeping pace with technological advances. It outlines how to apply the core principles of the AI White Paper to develop clear, evidence‑based regulatory frameworks for AI‑driven medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to position the organisation as the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user among defence bodies of its size. It focuses on leveraging AI to enhance operational capabilities, streamline processes, and maintain global leadership in defence technology.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to tap into the benefits of AI while carefully managing its risks. It sets out strategies, collaborations, and safeguards to promote safe, inclusive, and efficient AI use across transportation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright‑protected works are being used to train AI models, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights current practices, identifies challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing intellectual‑property rights with AI innovation.
